body: Pete Crow-Armstrong is the National League MVP, and it was not close. The Cubs center fielder received all 30 first-place votes and 420 points when the award was announced on Nov. 12, well ahead of Shohei Ohtani at 264 and Milwaukee's Brice Turang at 190.
At 24, in his third season, he played all 162 games, hit 45 home runs, stole 41 bases and finished with 9.8 WAR.
## Why fans are buying in

The season had something for every kind of fan. Crow-Armstrong hit .280 with a .570 slugging percentage, drove in 107 runs and scored 119. He led the majors in WAR, runs, home runs and total bases, and he became the seventh player in MLB history with a 40-40 season. He also won the Gold Glove in center field.

The win carries extra weight in Chicago. He is the first Cub to win the award since Kris Bryant in 2016 and joins a franchise list that includes Ernie Banks and Sammy Sosa. He also ended Ohtani's run of three straight MVP awards. In late October, his fellow players had already named him their Player of the Year.

In our analysis, a young star who does everything on the field, in one of baseball's most loyal markets, is the type of player whose jersey fans keep wearing for years. This is our view, not a sales figure.

body: Cade Cunningham just had the best scoring night of his career. He put up 52 points, 11 assists and five rebounds as the Pistons beat the Washington Wizards 144-140 in double overtime on Nov. 12, topping his old high of 46.
He did it without a single turnover, which no NBA player had done in a 50-point, 10-assist game since the league started tracking turnovers in 1977-78.
## Why fans are buying in

The efficiency stood out as much as the total. Cunningham made 16 of 25 shots and 17 of 18 free throws, and he scored 12 of his points across the two overtime periods, including the basket that put Detroit up four with about 25 seconds left.

The win also says a lot about where Detroit is headed. The Pistons moved to 8-3, and Ausar Thompson added a triple-double with 17 points, 11 rebounds and 11 assists. A team built around a young point guard and athletic wings is winning early, and Cunningham is the one with the ball in his hands at the end of games.

In our analysis, Cunningham has moved past the label of a promising former No. 1 pick and become the face of a team on the rise. Big nights like this one are what turn a local favorite into a jersey fans around the league want. This is our view, not a sales figure.
